fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Front Driveway; Access Drive; Vehicle Parking Area; Open Green Space; Landscaped Area; Perimeter Fencing
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Multiple Structures; Open Terrain
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responding units can confirm the correct property from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective posts on both sides to define the access point at night or in low-visibility conditions.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles along its full length so emergency vehicles can reach both structures without obstruction.
• Post the address visibly at the driveway entrance rather than only at the main residence, since the residence is not visible from the road on a long driveway.
• Identify and communicate the location of the detached structure to responding units, as it may not be immediately visible upon arrival.
• Keep a gate or entry point in the perimeter fencing unlocked or equipped with a key box so responders can enter without delay.
• Maintain the vehicle parking area clear of equipment or stored items that would block a responding unit from turning around or repositioning near the main residence.
• Trim any landscaping along the access drive that narrows the travel width or obscures sightlines for an approaching emergency vehicle.
• Designate a flat, stable area near the structures where responding units can stage equipment without crossing soft ground or landscaped areas.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Brush Area; Brush Area; Vegetation Near Structure; Open Terrain; Single Access Route; Limited Vegetation Separation; Scattered Trees; Ground Vegetation; Open Green Space
wildfire.recommendations:
• Remove shrubs that are growing directly next to the house.
• Thin scattered trees near the structure to create open space between their canopies and the building.
• Cut back ground vegetation growing close to the base of the structure.
• Clear brush from the area immediately surrounding the house, working outward to create open separation between the brush and the building.
• Mow or cut ground vegetation in the open green space areas nearest the structure to reduce the amount of low-lying plant material.
• Trim any tree branches that hang over or touch the roof or walls of the structure.
• Keep the single access route clear of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation along both sides.
• Remove dead or dry plant material from around any outbuildings or detached structures on the property.
• Separate shrub groupings by thinning or removing individual plants so fire cannot move easily from one group to the next toward the house.
• Keep the driveway surface and shoulders clear so emergency vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
